text: A pipeline report shows what is open. A forecast adds a promise: how much will actually close this period, and how confident are we? Let's see which native tools answer that.

Most Sales Cloud orgs have a Forecasts page that rolls amounts up the role or territory hierarchy. Managers see their team's numbers and can adjust them with a note. What you see depends on edition and setup, so treat this as one example. Use it for the weekly call: what is my number? Use reports when you need to slice further.

Three questions drive forecast analysis. Where will we land? Is there enough open pipeline? And was our forecast right last time? Each one needs a different report, and the third is the hardest. Keep them separate in your head, because a report that answers the first one rarely answers the third.

For the first question, report on Opportunities closing this quarter and group by Forecast Category. Sum the amount. Closed is your floor, Closed plus Commit is your call, and adding Best Case gives the stretch. Check whether the category follows the stage or reps edit it by hand. Some orgs let reps override the category by hand, which changes how far you can trust the ladder.

Coverage is open pipeline divided by the remaining target. Around three times is a common rule of thumb, but your win rate should set it. The catch is that quota isn't an Opportunity field, so analysts use a custom target field or a dashboard gauge goal. If you win only a quarter of your deals, you need more.
A forecast is only as good as the history behind it. Accuracy needs history, and native reports show today's data. Capture the commit number each period. Next up: lead conversion analysis.
